subject.title: fix: sleep tool — session-targeted wake, correct sandbox policy, doc fixes

question: Should `sleep` become a core agent tool, and if so should it be available across embedded and gateway runtimes without automatically joining existing `group:sessions` and coding-profile grants?
rationale: The PR creates a new core execution primitive and changes established tool-policy defaults; source inspection cannot determine the intended permanent runtime availability and authorization grouping.

options.title: Cross-runtime explicit tool
options.body: Add `sleep` consistently to embedded and gateway runs, require an explicit `sleep` grant initially, and document the policy before considering broader group membership.

options.title: Approve implicit default exposure
options.body: Intentionally include `sleep` in the coding profile and existing groups, document the compatibility impact, and prove both embedded and gateway behavior.

options.title: Decline core sleep
options.body: Keep cron and existing yield mechanisms as the supported primitives and close the core feature direction.

recommendation.title: Cross-runtime explicit tool
recommendation.body: Add `sleep` consistently to embedded and gateway runs, require an explicit `sleep` grant initially, and document the policy before considering broader group membership.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision extends the embedded `sessions_yield` lifecycle and tool-policy behavior most closely associated with their recent session-runtime work.
